Description: Flavius Bauto served in 374 AD as a distinguished Frankish cavalry commander and subsequent Magister militum of the Western Roman Empire. Operating under Valentinian I and Gratian, he commanded heavy comitatenses shock cavalry securing the Alpine passes and upper Danube valley. Appointed supreme military guardian and regent for young Valentinian II, he decisively repelled massive Alemannic incursions into Raetia and was honored with the ordinary consulship in 385 AD. Celebrated by Saint Ambrose and Emperor Theodosius the Great for his incorruptible integrity and martial fidelity, Bauto was also the father of Byzantine Empress Aelia Eudoxia. A master of frontier logistics, horse breeding, and armored cavalry maneuver, he maintained strict discipline across his garrisons, dedicated with unbending feudal devotion to shielding the Western Empire against existential barbarian ruin. Every dawn he personally inspected rampart palisades and cavalry bivouacs, ensuring that the western limes remained an impregnable bastion against the rising barbarian tide.
